name: Quick Chicken Stir Fry Bowls
desc: Pantry stir fry of thin-sliced chicken in a soy and sesame sauce with steam-in-bag vegetables over microwave rice.

source.evidence: Written for the owner in a claude.ai chat on 2026-09-15 from what was in the pantry; not adapted from a published recipe.

ingredients.raw: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced into thin strips
1/4 tsp ground black or white pepper
1 tbsp neutral oil, such as canola or avocado
1 tbsp oyster, hoisin, or teriyaki sauce
1 tsp honey or light brown sugar
1/2 tsp sriracha or red pepper flakes (optional)
1 tsp cornstarch (optional, for a thicker glaze)
1 (10 to 12 oz) bag frozen steam-in-bag stir fry vegetables
1 (8.5 oz) pouch 90-second white or jasmine rice
Sesame seeds and sliced green onion, for topping (optional)

steps: Toss the chicken strips with the garlic powder, ginger and pepper.
In a small bowl, stir together the soy sauce, oyster (or hoisin or teriyaki) sauce, honey, sesame oil, sriracha and cornstarch, if using, until the cornstarch dissolves.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook, flipping once, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, 5 to 7 min total.
While the chicken cooks, microwave the vegetables per the bag directions, but stop about 1 min early so they stay crisp.
Add the vegetables to the skillet, pour in the sauce, and toss over high heat until the sauce is glossy and slightly reduced, 1 to 2 min.
Squeeze the rice pouch to break up clumps, tear the vent, and microwave per the package, about 90 seconds.
Divide the rice between two bowls, top with the stir fry, and finish with sesame seeds and green onion, if using.
tips: Use whichever bottled sauce you have: oyster sauce is the most savory, hoisin the sweetest, and teriyaki can stand in for the honey.
Slicing the chicken thin keeps the sear short, so it stays juicy.
